rationale: The portfolio keeps its literal technical project management role visible while explaining why the operating work depends on participation, place, care, and memory. The About through-line connects Open House to contemporary and historical project evidence; the linked projects show concrete invitations, room practices, participant-shaped interfaces, and handoffs. The dated photographs work as evidence of inhabited settings, and their captions and permissions do not turn participants into testimonials. Three substantial continuities are reconstructable without exposing raw participant records.

The home viewport states the professional role. About names artistic, civic, technical, and social practice, explains systems people can inhabit, and links concrete work.
Project pages connect social settings and public interfaces to specific operating practices, with dated status, credits, and limits.

Open House initiation is distinct from collective governance; WOWList names Richard Caceres and community contributors; coalition outcomes remain collective. Sunday Dinner's exact image occurrence records human rights and represented-person review. Photo records distinguish staging permission from open production/indexing states.

The inspected public surfaces summarize the public Open House record without reproducing the article. The protected educational claim remains held with no public surfaces. threeProjectTrace.trace: Calendars made with Sunday Dinner become a lightweight, collaboratively editable publishing system using organizers' own language. Followable keyword communities, profiles, weekly email, and local calendars let distributed organizers shape and continue their scenes.
threeProjectTrace.boundary: Shared builder and organizer credit is explicit. Historical scale is not current use or measured community impact; the 2026 landing page is not represented as the full calendar returning.

threeProjectTrace.trace: Hospitality becomes repeatable through invitation, response, hosting, minimal documentation, and follow-up. Residency onboarding begins with the artist's inquiry, makes needs discussable, configures space, and hands off practical independence while leaving room for changed direction.
threeProjectTrace.boundary: The two specimens are explicitly redacted reconstructions. They describe workflow rather than artist outcomes, universal practice, participant consent, or an attendance database. Aggregate scale is not a claim about unique people.

threeProjectTrace.trace: Listening in cultural spaces becomes priority-setting, public event and campaign interfaces, practical sessions, town halls, hearings, and continuing action records. The Shoestring photograph and screen-to-room sequence make the social setting visible. The Wonderville guide demonstrates that attention to room layout and equipment remains part of current delivery.
threeProjectTrace.boundary: Jamie helped establish and produce a collective system. A delivered plan does not prove every cue occurred; event responses do not establish attendance; advocacy does not establish sole policy causation.

reading: The systems differ from conventional administration because participants' language, needs, physical settings, and ability to return shape the operating form. Documentation preserves a way to continue together.
